citation: Barron CI, Cook TJ. Effects of Variable Decompressions to 45,000 Feet. Aerosp Med. 1965;36(5):425–430.
locator: Methods pp. 426–427; Table I p. 427; Discussion and Summary p. 430 (PDF p. 6)
note: Four civilian test pilots and four passenger volunteers made eight experimental exposures. The report explicitly states that none experienced symptoms of aeroembolism. One case of barotitis required myringotomy. The separate 1955 Lockheed training report covers a different protocol and cohort scope.

citation: Marotte H, Toure C, Florence G, Lejeune D, Kerguelen M. Transport aircraft crew and decompression hazards: study of a positive pressure schedule. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1990;61(8):690–694.
locator: Subjects and Experimental Protocol p. 691 (PDF p. 2)
note: Eleven participants. One could not complete all tests due to significant dysbaric disturbances and was excluded from the physiological analysis. The protocol reports no observed aeroembolism symptoms. It does not give an outcome-evaluable count of people, sessions or altitude excursions.

citation: Marotte H, Toure C, Clere JM, Vieillefond H. Rapid decompression of a transport aircraft cabin: protection against hypoxia. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1990;61(1):21–27.
note: Ten volunteers and 105 rapid-decompression tests, including calibration tests. The exact number of participant exposures used in analysis and the number of clinical DCS events are unavailable.

citation: Holness DE, Porlier JAG, Ackles KN, Wright GR. Respiratory gas exchange during positive pressure breathing and rapid decompression to simulated altitudes of 18.3 and 24.4 km. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1980;51(5):454–458.
note: The 60,000-ft experiment reports seven participants and the 80,000-ft experiment reports two. The paper does not establish the number of actual runs or overlap of participants between experiments. DCS and VGE tallies are unavailable.

citation: Ernsting J, Green ID, Nagle RE, Wagner PR. High altitude protection from pressure-breathing mask with trunk and lower limb counterpressure. Aerosp Med. 1960;31(1):40–48.
locator: Experimental Methods pp. 41–42 and Series 3–4 p. 43 (PDF pp. 2–4)
note: The same five participants made both 56,000-ft chamber runs, one per configuration. Separate ground-level comparisons are outside that count. The paper describes loss of consciousness in two mask exposures. DCS and VGE tallies are unavailable.
